**My thinking:**

I've worked this land for over forty years. My family has always grown wheat and corn here in Quzhou — that's what the soil is good for, that's what the market buys, and that's what I know how to do. My two sons went to work in the city, so it's mostly me and my wife now. I can't manage too much land, but I won't reduce my plot either — I need the income.

Winter wheat goes in the ground every October, comes out in June. Then I turn around and plant summer corn right after. That's how my father did it, that's how everyone around here does it. No reason to change.

For seeds, I buy from the village cooperative shop — the same improved wheat variety I've been using for years (something like Jimai). For the corn I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958, because that's what works and everyone uses it. I wouldn't experiment with something new at my age.

I apply fertilizer generously. The crop needs to eat well to give a good harvest. I know the extension station people say to use less nitrogen, but I'd rather put a bit more and not worry. I've seen bad harvests from being stingy.

I pump water from the well three times for wheat — before winter freeze sets in, at jointing, and at heading. For corn, maybe twice if the rain doesn't come.

I spray herbicide after planting and maybe once more for insects. Nothing fancy.

After the corn harvest I plough deep. After the wheat I do rotary tillage before planting corn — quicker and the machine rental is cheaper.
